criteria.passage: I’d probably try to calm them down by saying we’ll have it sorted shortly and that I expect the team will get it closed in a day or so.
criteria.rationale: The candidate clearly states how they would communicate to the customer in understandable terms, outlining the message they would give.

criteria.passage: If we don’t have the cause yet, I’d still give them that estimate so they have something concrete.
criteria.rationale: This explicitly proposes giving a time estimate despite not knowing the cause or having a reliable resolution date, which is an unsupported promise and fails expectation management.

criteria.passage: I’d only reach back out if the final fix is ready, because I don’t want to keep giving them a bunch of half-updates.
criteria.rationale: The candidate proposes no intermediate status updates or confirmation mechanism, only contacting the customer when the final fix is ready, which is an inadequate follow-up approach in this scenario.
